entries.title: JST, 1 Chronicles 21:15. Compare 1 Chronicles 21:15 God stops an angel from destroying Jerusalem.
JST, 1 Corinthians 15:40. Compare 1 Corinthians 15:40 There are three degrees of glory in the Resurrection.

JST, 1 Corinthians 7:1–2, 5, 26, 29–33, 38. Compare 1 Corinthians 7:1–2, 5, 26, 29–38 Paul teaches that marriage is desirable. Those called as missionaries, however, serve God better if they remain single during their ministry.
JST, 1 John 2:1. Compare 1 John 2:1 Christ is our advocate with the Father if we repent.
JST, 1 John 3:9. Compare 1 John 3:9 Whoever is born of God does not continue in sin.
JST, 1 John 4:12. Compare 1 John 4:12 Only men who believe in God can see Him.
JST, 1 Peter 3:20. Compare 1 Peter 3:20 Some of the spirits in prison were unrighteous in the days of Noah.
JST, 1 Peter 4:6. Compare 1 Peter 4:6 The gospel is preached to those who are dead.
JST, 1 Samuel 16:14–16, 23. Compare 1 Samuel 16:14–16, 23 ; similar changes were made to 1 Samuel 18:10 and 19:9 The evil spirit that comes upon Saul is not from the Lord.
JST, 1 Thessalonians 4:15. Compare 1 Thessalonians 4:15 Those righteous people who are alive at the coming of the Lord will have no advantage over the righteous dead.
JST, 1 Timothy 2:4. Compare 1 Timothy 2:4 Christ is the Only Begotten Son and Mediator.

JST, 1 Timothy 3:15–16. Compare 1 Timothy 3:15–16 The Church is founded on the central principle that Jesus became mortal, taught the gospel, and returned to His Father. Note: The subtle change in the following verses emphasizes that the “pillar and ground of the truth” is Jesus Christ.
JST, 1 Timothy 6:15–16. Compare 1 Timothy 6:15–16 Those who have the light of immortality (the gospel) dwelling in them can see Jesus.
JST, 2 Chronicles 18:22. Compare 2 Chronicles 18:22 The Lord does not put a lying spirit into the mouths of prophets.
JST, 2 Corinthians 5:16. Compare 2 Corinthians 5:16 Paul counsels Saints not to live after the manner of the flesh.

JST, 2 Peter 3:3–13. Compare 2 Peter 3:3–13 In the last days, many people will deny the Lord Jesus Christ. When He comes, many natural calamities will happen. If we endure in righteousness, we will receive a new earth.
JST, 2 Samuel 12:13. Compare 2 Samuel 12:13 David’s grievous sin is not put away by God.
JST, 2 Thessalonians 2:2–3, 7–9. Compare 2 Thessalonians 2:2–9 Satan will cause a falling away or apostasy before the Lord returns.
JST, Acts 22:29–30. Compare Acts 22:29–30 The chief captain loosed Paul from his bands.
JST, Acts 9:7. Compare Acts 9:7 ; 22:9 Those who are with Paul at his conversion see the light, but they do not hear the voice or see the Lord.
JST, Amos 7:3. Compare Amos 7:3 The Lord does not repent; men repent.
JST, Colossians 2:21–22. Compare Colossians 2:20–23 The commandments of men might have value in teaching such things as self-discipline, but they neither honor God nor save man.
JST, Deuteronomy 10:2. Compare Deuteronomy 10:2 On the first set of tablets God reveals the everlasting covenant of the holy priesthood.
JST, Ephesians 4:26. Compare Ephesians 4:26 Unrighteous anger is sin.
JST, Exodus 18:1. Compare Exodus 18:1 Jethro is a high priest.
JST, Exodus 22:18. Compare Exodus 22:18 Murderers shall not live.
JST, Exodus 32:14. Compare Exodus 32:14 The Lord will spare the Israelites who will repent.
JST, Exodus 33:20, 23. Compare Exodus 33:20, 23 No sinful man can see God’s face and live.
JST, Exodus 34:1–2, 14. Compare Exodus 34:1–2, 14 ; D&C 84:21–26

JST, Exodus 4:21. Compare Exodus 4:21 ; 7:3, 13 ; 9:12 ; 10:1, 20, 27 ; 11:10 ; 14:4, 8, 17 ; Deuteronomy 2:30 The Lord is not responsible for Pharaoh’s hardness of heart. See also JST, Exodus 7:3, 13 ; 9:12 ; 10:1, 20, 27 ; 11:10 ; 14:4, 8, 17 ; each reference, when correctly translated, shows that Pharaoh hardened his own heart.
JST, Galatians 3:19–20. Compare Galatians 3:19–20 Moses is the mediator of the first covenant, or the law. Jesus Christ is the mediator of the new covenant.
JST, Genesis 14:25–40. Compare Genesis 14:18–20 Melchizedek blesses Abram. Melchizedek’s great ministry and the powers and blessings of the Melchizedek Priesthood are described.
JST, Genesis 15:9–12. Compare Genesis 15:1–6 Abraham learns of the Resurrection and sees a vision of Jesus’ mortal ministry.

JST, Genesis 17:3–12. Compare Genesis 17:3–12 The people fail to obey the gospel ordinances, including baptism. God explains to Abraham the covenant of circumcision and the age of accountability of children.
JST, Genesis 19:9–15. Compare Genesis 19:8–10 Lot resists the wickedness of Sodom, and angels protect him.
JST, Genesis 1:1–8:18. Compare Genesis 1:1–6:13 This text of the Bible was restored by Joseph Smith and is published in the Pearl of Great Price as Selections from the Book of Moses .
JST, Genesis 21:31–32. Compare Genesis 21:32–34 Abraham worships the everlasting God.

JST, Genesis 48:5–11. Compare Genesis 48:5–6 Ephraim and Manasseh become tribes of Israel. Just as ancient Joseph saved his family temporally, his descendants will save Israel spiritually in the latter days.

JST, Genesis 50:24–38. Compare Genesis 50:24–26 ; 2 Nephi 3:4–22 Joseph in Egypt prophesies of Moses freeing Israel from Egyptian bondage; of a branch of Joseph’s descendants being led to a faraway land, where they will be remembered in the covenants of the Lord; of God calling a latter-day prophet named Joseph to join the records of Judah and of Joseph; and of Aaron serving as a spokesman for Moses.
JST, Genesis 9:4–6. Compare Genesis 8:20–22 After the Flood, Noah asks the Lord not to curse the earth again.
JST, Hebrews 11:1. Compare Hebrews 11:1 Faith is the assurance of things hoped for.
JST, Hebrews 1:6–7. Compare Hebrews 1:6–7 Angels are ministering spirits.
JST, Hebrews 4:3. Compare Hebrews 4:3 Those who harden their hearts will not be saved; those who repent will enter into the Lord’s rest.
JST, Hebrews 6:1–10. Compare Hebrews 6:1–10 The principles of Christ’s doctrine lead to perfection.
JST, Hebrews 7:3. Compare Hebrews 7:3 Melchizedek was a priest after the order of the Son of God. All those who receive this priesthood can become like the Son of God.

JST, Isaiah 29:1–8. Compare Isaiah 29:1–8 The messages formerly preached in Jerusalem by ancient prophets will in the latter days be preached from the Book of Mormon, which came forth “out of the ground.”
JST, Isaiah 42:19–23. Compare Isaiah 42:19–22 The Lord sends His servant to teach those who have chosen not to see or hear the truth; those who listen and obey will be made perfect.
JST, James 1:2. Compare James 1:2 Afflictions, not temptations, help to sanctify us.
JST, James 2:1. Compare James 2:1 Members should not regard one person more highly than another.
JST, Jeremiah 26:13. Compare Jeremiah 26:13 The Lord does not repent; men repent.
JST, John 13:8–10. Compare John 13:8–10 Jesus washes the feet of the Apostles to fulfill the law of the Jews.
JST, John 14:30. Compare John 14:30 The prince of darkness, or Satan, is of this world.

JST, John 1:1–34. Compare John 1:1–34 The gospel of Jesus Christ has been preached from the beginning. John the Baptist is the Elias who prepares the way for Christ, and Jesus Christ is the Elias who restores all things and through whom salvation comes.
JST, John 4:1–4. Compare John 4:1–2 The Pharisees desire to kill Jesus. He performs some baptisms, but His disciples perform more.
JST, John 6:44. Compare John 6:44 The Father’s will is that all receive Jesus. Those who do the will of Jesus will be raised in the resurrection of the just.
JST, Luke 11:53. Compare Luke 11:52 The fulness of the scriptures is the key of knowledge.
JST, Luke 12:9–12. Compare Luke 12:9–10 ; see also JST, Matthew 12:37–38 and D&C 132:26–27 Jesus explains that blasphemy against the Holy Ghost will not be forgiven.
JST, Luke 14:35–37. Compare Luke 14:34 Those who know Moses and the prophets believe in Jesus.
JST, Luke 16:16–23. Compare Luke 16:16–18 The law and the prophets testify of Jesus. The Pharisees seek to destroy the kingdom. Jesus introduces the parable of the rich man and Lazarus.
JST, Luke 17:21. Compare Luke 17:20–21 The kingdom of God has already come.
JST, Luke 18:27. Compare Luke 18:27 Trusting in riches prevents a person from entering the kingdom of God.
JST, Luke 1:8. Compare Luke 1:8 Zacharias, John the Baptist’s father, performs priesthood duties.
JST, Luke 21:24–26. Compare Luke 21:25–26 Jesus speaks of some signs of His coming.
JST, Luke 23:35. Compare Luke 23:34 Jesus asks forgiveness for the Roman soldiers who are crucifying Him.
JST, Luke 24:2–4. Compare Luke 24:2–5 The women see two angels at Jesus’ sepulcher.
JST, Luke 2:46. Compare Luke 2:46 The doctors in the temple listen to Jesus and ask Him questions.
JST, Luke 3:4–11. Compare Luke 3:4–6 Christ will come as prophesied to bring salvation to Israel and to the Gentiles. In the fulness of times, He will come again to judge the world.
JST, Luke 6:29–30. Compare Luke 6:29–30 Jesus teaches that it is better to endure persecution than to contend with an enemy.
JST, Luke 9:24–25. Compare Luke 9:24–25 Gaining worldly wealth is not worth losing one’s soul.
JST, Mark 12:32. Compare Mark 12:27 God is not a God of the dead, because He raises the dead from their graves.
JST, Mark 14:20–26. Compare Mark 14:22–25 Jesus institutes the sacrament in remembrance of His body and blood.
JST, Mark 16:3–6. Compare Mark 16:4–7 ; Luke 24:2–4 Two angels greet the women at the tomb of the Savior.
JST, Mark 2:26–27. Compare Mark 2:27–28 The Son of Man is Lord of the Sabbath because He made the Sabbath day.
JST, Mark 3:21–25. Compare Mark 3:28–30 Jesus will forgive all sinners who repent except those who blaspheme against the Holy Ghost.
JST, Mark 7:10–12. Compare Mark 7:10 Jesus condemns those who reject the prophets and do not obey the law of Moses.
JST, Mark 8:37–38. Compare Mark 8:35 Whoever is willing to die for Jesus’ sake will receive salvation.
JST, Mark 9:3. Compare Mark 9:4 John the Baptist is on the Mount of Transfiguration.
JST, Matthew 11:13–15. Compare Matthew 11:10–11, 13–14 John the Baptist is the Elias who would come to prepare the way for the Savior.
JST, Matthew 12:37–38. Compare Matthew 12:43–44 ; see also JST, Luke 12:9–12 Whosoever speaks against the Holy Ghost will not be forgiven.

JST, Matthew 13:39–44. Compare Matthew 13:39–42 ; see also D&C 86:1–7 Before the end of the world (the destruction of the wicked), messengers sent of heaven will gather the righteous from among the wicked.
JST, Matthew 16:25–29. Compare Matthew 16:24–26 Jesus explains what it means “to take up one’s cross”: to deny all ungodliness and every worldly lust and to keep His commandments.
JST, Matthew 17:10–14. Compare Matthew 17:11–13 Jesus teaches of two Eliases—one to prepare and another to restore.
JST, Matthew 18:11. Compare Matthew 18:11 ; see also Moroni 8 Little children have no need of repentance.
JST, Matthew 19:13. Compare Matthew 19:13 Little children will be saved.
JST, Matthew 21:33. Compare Matthew 21:32–33 Man must repent before he can believe in Christ.
JST, Matthew 23:6. Compare Matthew 23:9 He who is in heaven is our creator.
JST, Matthew 26:22, 24–25. Compare Matthew 26:26–28 ; JST, Mark 14:20–25 Jesus first breaks the sacramental bread then blesses it. The sacrament is in remembrance of Jesus’ body and blood.
JST, Matthew 27:3–6. Compare Matthew 27:3–5 ; Acts 1:18 Judas’s death is described.
JST, Matthew 3:4–6. Compare Matthew 2:4–6 The prophets foretold that Bethlehem would be the place of the Messiah’s birth.
JST, Matthew 4:1, 5–6, 8–9. Compare Matthew 4:1, 5–6, 8–9 ; similar changes were made in Luke 4:2, 5–11 Jesus is led by the Spirit, not by Satan.
JST, Matthew 5:21. Compare Matthew 5:19 Whoso keeps the commandments and teaches others to do the same will be saved.
JST, Matthew 6:14. Compare Matthew 6:13 ; similar changes were made in Luke 11:4 The Lord does not lead us into temptation.
JST, Matthew 7:1–2. Compare Matthew 7:1–2 Judge not unrighteously.
JST, Matthew 9:18–21. Compare Matthew 9:16–17 Jesus rejects the baptism of the Pharisees; it has no value because they do not accept Him. He proclaims that He is the one who gave the law of Moses.
JST, Psalm 109:4. Compare Psalm 109:4 We are to pray for our adversaries.
JST, Psalm 11:1–5. Compare Psalm 11:1–5 In the last days the righteous will flee to the mountain of the Lord. When the Lord comes, He will destroy the wicked and redeem the righteous.
JST, Psalm 14:1–7. Compare Psalm 14:1–7 The Psalmist sees the loss of truth in the last days and looks forward to the establishment of Zion.
JST, Psalm 24:7–10. Compare Psalm 24:7–10 The King of Glory will redeem His people at His coming.

JST, Revelation 12:1–17. Compare Revelation 12:1–17 John explains the symbols of the woman, the child, the rod of iron, the dragon, and Michael. The war that began in heaven is continued on the earth. Note the changed sequence of verses in the JST .
JST, Revelation 19:15, 21. Compare Revelation 19:15, 21 God uses the word of Christ to smite the nations.
JST, Revelation 1:1–8. Compare Revelation 1:1–8 John the Apostle receives the prophecies in the book of Revelation. He is visited by Jesus Christ and by an angel.
JST, Revelation 2:22. Compare Revelation 2:22 The wicked are cast into hell.
JST, Revelation 5:6. Compare Revelation 5:6 Twelve servants of God are sent to all the earth.
JST, Romans 13:6–7. Compare Romans 13:6–7 Those who honor civil authorities make their honor to God greater and more perfect.
JST, Romans 3:5–8. Compare Romans 3:5–8 Paul teaches that a person cannot do evil to bring about good.
JST, Romans 4:2–5. Compare Romans 4:2–5 Man can only be saved by the grace of Jesus Christ, not by works related to observance of the law of Moses.
JST, Romans 7:5–27. Compare Romans 7:5–25 Only Christ has power to permanently change men’s souls for good.
JST, Romans 8:8. Compare Romans 8:8 Those who follow after the ways of the flesh cannot please God.
Selections from the Joseph Smith Translation of the Bible
